decisions.reason: Archiving and reporting software close to the core offer has its own website page and fits the move toward data-driven infrastructure management, so with no sign of a shortfall against aspirations there is no trigger for problemistic search.

This second archiving product is only mentioned on the website and may overlap with Product A, which raises some risk of consolidation, but its low marginal cost and the firm's slack make keeping it the more likely choice.
The manhole door with integrated railing builds on established hardware, has a page of its own, and meets steady municipal safety demand, so its results likely meet aspirations.

The floating sludge extractor is a niche extension of the firm's wastewater equipment and is only mentioned online, but it costs little to carry, so slack lets the firm retain it while its results are still uncertain.
Control technology for water engineering machinery is central to the firm's integrated automation strategy, so dropping it is unlikely without clear underperformance.
